learning_objective: 🎯 Explore what constitutes a just society, understand different principles of justice, and dive into John Rawls' fascinating 'Veil of Ignorance'!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Justice is about giving everyone what is due to them. In modern times, it means creating a society where people have fair opportunities and basic minimum living conditions.
1. Equal treatment for equals (no discrimination). 2. Proportionate justice (rewarding people based on effort/skill). 3. Recognition of special needs (helping those who are disadvantaged).

main_concepts.concept_title: blindfold John Rawls' Theory of Justice
main_concepts.simple_explanation: Rawls asks us to imagine a 'Veil of Ignorance'—if you had to design society without knowing if you would be rich, poor, healthy, or disabled in it, you would naturally design a fair society that protects the weakest.
A just society must provide its members with basic minimum conditions (food, housing, clean water, education) to enable them to compete on equal terms.
The debate over whether the free market provides justice (by rewarding hard work) or if state intervention is necessary to protect the poor and vulnerable.

fun_activity.title: 🙈 The Veil of Ignorance Game
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine you are making rules for a new planet. You don't know if you will be born smart, disabled, rich, or poor there. Write down 3 laws you would make to ensure you survive comfortably no matter who you end up being!

exam_tips: 📌 John Rawls' 'Veil of Ignorance' is a highly important concept. Practice explaining it in your own words.
📌 Remember the three principles of justice: equal treatment, proportionate justice, and special needs.
📌 Understand that justice often requires balancing these three principles against each other.
quick_recap: ⭐ The ancient Indian concept of Dharma is closely related to justice.
⭐ Proportionate justice explains why a highly skilled surgeon might be paid more than a clerk, as long as basic needs for both are met.
⭐ Social justice requires state intervention to ensure a basic minimum standard of living for all citizens.
